title: Athena: wisdom and craft
text: Athena is associated with wisdom, practical skill, crafts, and strategic warfare. Greek myths often distinguish her strategic approach to conflict from Ares' connection with violent warfare. The owl and olive tree are traditional symbols associated with Athena.
source_note: Original short editorial summary; consult the linked classical quotations for verification.

title: Athena: unusual birth
text: In a well-known Greek myth, Athena emerges from the head of Zeus, fully grown and armed. Versions of divine genealogies vary across ancient authors.
source_note: Original short editorial summary; myths have multiple versions.

title: Zeus: sky and kingship
text: Zeus is the king of the Olympian gods and is strongly associated with the sky, thunder, lightning, and divine authority. He is a son of the Titans Cronus and Rhea.

title: Hera: marriage and queenship
text: Hera is queen of the Olympian gods, wife of Zeus, and a goddess associated with marriage and women. Greek myths also describe disputes surrounding Zeus's affairs.

title: Apollo and Artemis: siblings
text: Apollo and Artemis are twins in Greek myth, children of Zeus and Leto. Apollo is associated with prophecy, music, and healing; Artemis is associated with hunting, wildlife, and young animals.
source_note: Original short editorial summary; see also the Apollo entry.

title: Apollo: prophecy at Delphi
text: Apollo is associated with music, prophecy, archery, and healing. His oracle at Delphi is one of the best-known centers of prophecy in Greek tradition.

title: Hermes: messenger and travelers
text: Hermes is the messenger of the Olympian gods. He is associated with travel, trade, language, and guiding souls to the underworld. Winged sandals and a herald's staff are among his attributes.

title: Demeter and Persephone: the seasons
text: Demeter is the goddess of grain and agriculture and the mother of Persephone. A major myth describes Persephone's removal to the underworld and Demeter's grief; their reunion is connected to the seasonal cycle. Details differ among ancient sources.
source_note: Original short editorial summary; the Homeric Hymn to Demeter is a major ancient source.

title: Hades: ruler of the underworld
text: Hades rules the underworld and is a brother of Zeus and Poseidon. Persephone becomes his consort in one important myth. Hades is not the same as Thanatos, the personification of death.

title: Poseidon: seas and earthquakes
text: Poseidon is a god of the sea, earthquakes, and horses. His trident is a traditional emblem. He is a brother of Zeus and Hades.

title: Ares: warfare
text: Ares is a god associated with battle, violence, and the destructive side of war. He is commonly contrasted with Athena, who represents strategic and disciplined warfare.

title: Aphrodite: love and desire
text: Aphrodite is a goddess associated with love, beauty, and desire. Her origins are presented differently in ancient traditions; some accounts describe her birth from sea foam.

title: Hephaestus: craftsmanship and fire
text: Hephaestus is a god associated with metalworking, the forge, and skilled craftsmanship. Greek myths credit him with making extraordinary objects for gods and heroes.

title: Dionysus: wine and theatre
text: Dionysus is associated with wine, ecstatic celebration, and theatre. In Greek religion and myth, his worship appears in various ritual traditions and dramatic festivals.

title: Hestia: hearth and home
text: Hestia is the goddess associated with the hearth and the home's sacred fire. She is traditionally described as a sister of Zeus, Hera, Demeter, Hades, and Poseidon.

title: Hecate: crossroads and magic
text: Hecate is associated with crossroads, torches, and certain forms of magic in Greek tradition. She appears in the story of Demeter's search for Persephone.

title: Nike: victory
text: Nike is the personification of victory and is often shown winged. In ancient art she appears alongside other deities, including Athena and Zeus.

title: Hypnos: sleep
text: Hypnos is the personification of sleep in Greek mythology. He is frequently linked with his brother Thanatos, the personification of death.
